summary: Nobuyuki Watase is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed a master's at Kyoto University (~1964–1966). He served as associate professor at Tokai University (~1984–2007) and president of Kobe Shukugawa Gakuin University (~2007–2011).

Nobuyuki Yamagiwa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a lecturer post at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2002), taught Shayne Clarke, and is attested as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Otani University (~1959–1963) under Issai Funahashi and doctoral supervisor Genjun Sasaki. He was a JSPS research fellow (1972) and held assistant, lecturer, and research appointments at Otani University.

Nolan Pliny Jacobson was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago in 1948 after studying at Emory University. He served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Winthrop University (1954–1974).

Noopur Shalini works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at NIFT, IGNOU, Ningbo University, and the University of Mumbai, she held a position in the Department of Archaeology at Zhejiang University in 2023.

Nora Kershaw Chadwick was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1911–1915). She held academic posts at the University of St Andrews (~1919–1923) and the University of Cambridge (~1950–1958).

Norbert M. Samuelson was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his doctorate at Indiana University under Shlomo Pines. He taught notably as professor at Temple University (1975–1998) and later at Arizona State University.

Noriaki Hakamaya is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Shun'ei Hirai and Zuiho Yamaguchi, later serving as professor at Komazawa University (1985–2011).

Noriaki Hosoda is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as an assistant (attested 1986) and associate professor (attested 2003) at Hokkaido University, and is attested as a professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.
Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University from ~1949 to ~1953. He later served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1982).

Norihiko Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Osaka Kyoiku University, Bukkyo University, and Visva-Bharati University. He spent his career at Bukkyo University, serving as lecturer (1976), associate professor (1982), professor (1994, 2013), and emeritus professor (2015–2021).
Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held an assistant post at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1962).
Norihiro Matsuura is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as faculty at both Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

Norihisa Baba is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hanazono University and under Masahiro Shimoda at the University of Tokyo. He has served as professor at the University of Tokyo and its Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia.

Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 2014) and representative of the Matsunami Seiren Sensei Koki Kinenkai (attested 2007).

Noritoshi Aramaki is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from Kyoto University. He served as associate professor and professor at Kyoto University, associate professor at Osaka University, and professor at Otani University (~2000–2007).

Noriyuki Kudo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University and later became an associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2026).

Norman Brooke Jopson was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cambridge, Vienna (under Paul Kretschmer), Charles University, and Saint Petersburg. He served as Reader at King's College London and Professor of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1937–1955).

Norman Cutler was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Michigan, University of Washington, and University of Chicago under A. K. Ramanujan, later serving as assistant professor at the University of Chicago (~1979–2002).

Norman Fischer is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Colgate, Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, training under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. He founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.
